>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
On the eve of midterm election day, President Trump delivered his closing message for Republicans
at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
>> We've done a great job here, though, that people from interior have been incredible.
And the pool is now better and more beautiful than it's ever been before.
>> The President spent some 20 minutes talking about his renovation projects in the nation's
capital before casting Democrats as dangerous radicals.
Tens of billions of Americans have already cast an early or absentee ballot.
Latino voters will be a key demographic to watch in several races across the country
as NPR's Domenico Montanaro reports.
>> Latinos have soured on President Trump in the second term.
His approval ratings with the group are low, and they make up large portions of lots of
congressional districts.
Particularly important to watch is gonna be South Florida and South Texas.
Trump won over many Latinos in those places in the 2024 presidential election, but because
of the cost of living and harsh deportation tactics, there are signs they are either going
to swing back to Democrats or stay home.
Either way, Democrats need to flip three seats to win control of the House, and there are
at least 20 targeted districts where Latinos make up at least one in five people, making
them a critical group to watch, Domenico Montanaro, NPR News, Washington.
>> A federal judge has dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit against Harvard University.
The Justice Department had sought to force Harvard to turn over records for an investigation
into whether the school continues to consider race in its admissions process.
But the judge in the case said Monday that the department did not take the necessary
procedural step to get the records before filing the lawsuit.
North Korea, denying it was behind last week's theft of more than $6 billion from Binance,
the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul on what's
believed to be the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
>> In a statement carried by state media, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's sister Kim
Yeo Jong called the FBI's Saturday announcement that Pyongyang was behind the hack, a political
provocation, absurd rhetoric, and proof of the U.S.'s hostile policies towards Pyongyang.
She added that North Korea's consistent policy is to oppose malicious acts in cyberspace.
The FBI attributed the hack to Traitor Traitor, a sub-unit of cyber operatives under North
Korean military intelligence.
The FBI and crypto researchers observed the hackers unauthorized transactions in public
blockchain records, and listed the addresses of accounts linked to North Korea, which received
the transferred funds.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
>> Ukrainian authorities say more than two dozen people were killed in the Russian bombing
of an aid distribution center and a nearby shelter in southern Ukraine.
The attacks came after a limited ceasefire expired Monday in a different region in the
country's south.
This is NPR News.
New York State has reported its first death linked to measles in more than 30 years.
State health officials said Monday that a child died in rural Lewis County in northern
New York.
The death comes as the U.S. experiences its worst measles resurgence in decades.
Pennsylvania has been the epicenter of the outbreak, reporting more than 1,400 confirmed
cases and five measles-associated deaths so far this year.
Federal investigators say parts of a business jet may have broken off before it crashed
in south Florida.
On Sunday, all nine people on board were killed, NPR's Joel Rose reports.
>> Video recorded by witnesses captured the rapid nosedive and the fiery explosion on
impact near West Palm Beach.
National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman says investigators are trying
to understand why the Learjet crashed on its way from Austin to the Bahamas.
>> We do have some evidence that there was some breakup of the aircraft before impact.
We're still seeking to determine that.
>> Chapman says the weather will be a major focus of the investigation.
As one of the pilots reported icy conditions at high altitude moments before the nosedive
began.
Multiple media outlets reported that a 20-year-old Florida woman was one of the two pilots, though
NPR has not independently confirmed that.
Joel Rose, NPR News.
>> Asian stock markets mixed in Tuesday trading markets in Tokyo closed for a holiday, but
shares in South Korea and Taiwan are down more than 3% following a sell-off on Wall
Street.
The prices for Nvidia and Google parent Alphabet dragged down the S&P 500, which fell half
a percentage point.
The Dow closed up for a tenth of a percent.
I'm Joel Snyder, NPR News.
